title: “Rādha, whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all form should…
content: “Rādha, whatever form there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all form should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Whatever feeling … perception … formations … consciousness there is, past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near — all consciousness should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Rādha, knowing thus, seeing thus, regarding this conscious body and all external signs, there is no ‘I-making, mine-making, or underlying tendency to conceit.’”

title: “Again, the five kinds of kings Are present in the world — Learn to subdue them, Always keeping mindfulness. Toward forms and sounds, Toward tastes…
content:
“Again, the five kinds of kings
Are present in the world —
Learn to subdue them,
Always keeping mindfulness.
Toward forms and sounds,
Toward tastes and smells,
And toward contacts —
Subdue desire and lust.

Subdue desire
For these things.
The mindful monk,
With mind well liberated,
Then, at the right time,
Rightly reflecting on the Dhamma,
With unified mind,
He should destroy darkness.” So spoke the Blessed One.

title: - What is called the wrong path? What destroys day and night? What defiles the holy life? What is a bath without water? - Greed…
content:
- What is called the wrong path?
What destroys day and night?
What defiles the holy life?
What is a bath without water?
- Greed is called the wrong path,
Aging destroys day and night,
Women defile the holy life,
Ensnaring humankind —
Austerities and the holy life
Are a bath without water.

title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to completion, as wise…
content: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to completion, as wise attention. Through wise attention, monks, unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to full development.”

title: “Venerable sir, what is the first jhāna?” “Here, venerable sir, a monk, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the…
content: “Venerable sir, what is the first jhāna?” “Here, venerable sir, a monk, secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, enters and dwells in the first jhāna, accompanied by initial and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion. This, venerable sir, is called the first jhāna.” “Venerable sir, how many factors does the first jhāna have?” “Venerable sir, the first jhāna has five factors. Here, a monk in the first jhāna has initial thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and unification of mind. Thus, venerable sir, the first jhāna has five factors.” “Venerable sir, how many factors does the first jhāna abandon and how many does it possess?” “Venerable sir, the first jhāna abandons five factors and possesses five factors. Here, a monk in the first jhāna has abandoned sensual desire, abandoned ill-will, abandoned sloth and torpor, abandoned restlessness and remorse, abandoned doubt; he possesses initial thought, sustained thought, rapture, pleasure, and unification of mind. Thus, venerable sir, the first jhāna abandons five factors and possesses five factors.”

title: “Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for form — abandon it. Thus that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made…
content: “Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for form — abandon it. Thus that form will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future. Regarding feeling … perception … formations … Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving there is for consciousness — abandon it. Thus that consciousness will be abandoned, cut off at the root, made like a palm stump, made non-existent, so that it cannot arise again in the future.”

title: “Monks, for a clansman who has gone forth out of faith, this is the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma: dwell often in disenchantment toward…
content: “Monks, for a clansman who has gone forth out of faith, this is the Dhamma in accordance with the Dhamma: dwell often in disenchantment toward form … toward feeling … toward perception … toward formations, dwell often in disenchantment toward consciousness. One who dwells often in disenchantment toward form … toward consciousness fully understands form … feeling … perception … formations … fully understands consciousness. One who fully understands form, fully understands feeling, fully understands perception, fully understands formations, fully understands consciousness, is freed from form, freed from feeling, freed from perception, freed from formations, freed from consciousness, freed from birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is freed from suffering.”

title: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can…
content: “Venerable sir, thus a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected: ‘He will attend to the sign of the beautiful. By attending to the sign of the beautiful, greed will pollute his mind. He will die with greed, with ill-will, with delusion, with stain, his mind polluted.’”

title: “The stream of craving flows everywhere, The creeper of craving sprouts and stands. Seeing that creeper that has arisen, Cut its root with wisdom.” “People,…
content:
“The stream of craving flows everywhere,
The creeper of craving sprouts and stands.
Seeing that creeper that has arisen,
Cut its root with wisdom.”

“People, immersed in sensual pleasures,
Delight in various pleasures.
Though they seek happiness,
They undergo birth and aging.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Bound by craving,
They undergo suffering for a long time.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Therefore, a monk who desires his own dispassion
Should abandon craving.”

title: “One who has cut off craving, Without remainder, Dried up the swift stream — That monk abandons the near and far shore, Like a serpent…
content:
“One who has cut off craving,
Without remainder,
Dried up the swift stream —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One who has destroyed conceit,
Without remainder,
As a great flood destroys a fragile reed —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”
